NUM	<p>28fb_bbfa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5c6400;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5c6400;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c6400;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #05639e;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #05639e;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #05639e;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3b7a;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8b3b7a;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8b3b7a;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, erx, +++, erx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #386d1e;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #386d1e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #386d1e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006885;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006885;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8b3b7a;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8b3b7a;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8c491e;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8c491e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c491e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276d4a;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276d4a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276d4a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5f49b4;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5f49b4;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5f49b4;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, nty, +++, nty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8c491e;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8c491e;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8c491e;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d60;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d60;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d60;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3958ae;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3958ae;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3958ae;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, frx, +++, frx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e362c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5c6400;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5c6400;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. NUM	<p>810d_8eb4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e362c;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e362c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e362c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5c6400;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5c6400;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5c6400;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #05639e;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #05639e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #05639e;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mpx, +++, mpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
